children: are set to report quarterly results this week, with investors looking for revenue growth and updates on profitability amid diverging analyst estimate revisions.

UPS will report third-quarter earnings before the market opens on Tuesday, October 27. Analysts expect EPS of $1.62, down 6.9% year over year, while revenue is forecast to rise 4.1% to $22.28B. UPS has beaten both earnings and revenue estimates in 88% of reporting periods over the past two years. However, earnings expectations have weakened in recent months, with two upward and 22 downward EPS estimate revisions over the past three months. Revenue estimates have been more positive, with 16 upward revisions and two downward revisions.

FedEx is scheduled to report Q3 CY26 earnings after the market closes on Wednesday, October 28. Analysts expect EPS of $3.38, down 25.1% year over year, while revenue is projected to increase 1.8% to $22.6B. FedEx has beaten both earnings and revenue estimates 75% of the time over the past two years. In the past three months, EPS estimates have seen two upward and two downward revisions, while revenue estimates have had one upward and two downward revisions.
Both stocks carry a Hold Quant rating. FedEx is up approximately 4% year-to-date, while UPS has gained just 0.9% - both underperforming the 12% gain in SP500.

Investors will focus on shipping demand, operating costs, efficiency initiatives, and management outlooks for the remainder of the year. The sharp projected decline in FedEx earnings makes its profitability outlook a key point of attention, while UPS faces a more modest expected EPS decline alongside stronger projected revenue growth.

United Parcel Service as Hold, with shares trading near prior lows and limited upside despite slight undervaluation. He expects investors to focus on fuel costs and operating expenses, though efficiency gains could help offset these pressures. Schönberger also highlighted automation, noting that 68.5% of packages were routed through automated facilities, where delivery costs are about 28% lower per package.

FedEx a Hold, with shares at around $291 trading close to his estimated intrinsic value of $300. He sees improving domestic margins, efficiency gains from Network 2.0 and lower capital intensity supporting stronger cash generation following the Freight spin-off. However, Bailey said international margins remain a concern, with further improvement in Europe needed to justify the current valuation.
